items.type: {V : Type u_14} → {E : Type u_15} → [LineDeriv V E E] → {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → V) → E → E
items.informal_description: For a natural number $n$, this function takes a sequence of $n$ elements from $V$ and an element of $E$, and returns the composition of $n$ successive linear derivative operations. It is defined recursively: for $n=0$ it acts as the identity, and for $n+1$ it composes the linear derivative operation applied to the first element with the iterated derivative of the remaining $n$ elements.

items.informal_name: Composition of Hasse Derivatives on Laurent Series
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {V : Type u_2} [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module R V] (k l : ℕ)
  (f : LaurentSeries V),
  (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R k) ((LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R l) f) =
    (k + l).choose k • (LaurentSeries.hasseDeriv R (k + l)) f
items.informal_description: For any natural numbers $k$ and $l$, and any Laurent series $f$ with coefficients in an $R$-module $V$, the composition of the Hasse derivatives of orders $k$ and $l$ applied to $f$ equals $\binom{k + l}{k} \cdot \text{hasseDeriv}_{k + l}(f)$, where $\text{hasseDeriv}_n(f)$ denotes the Hasse derivative of order $n$.

items.informal_name: Successor Case for Iterated Linear Derivatives
items.type:
∀ {V : Type u_14} {E : Type u_15} [inst : LineDeriv V E E] {n : ℕ} (m : Fin (n + 1) → V) (f : E),
  LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp m f = LineDeriv.lineDerivOp (m 0) (LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp (Fin.tail m) f)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, function $m : \mathrm{Fin}(n+1) \to V$, and element $f \in E$, the $n$-th iterated linear derivative $\partial^{m} f$ equals the linear derivative $\partial_{m(0)}$ applied to the $(n-1)$-th iterated derivative $\partial^{\mathrm{tail}(m)} f$, where $\mathrm{tail}(m)$ discards the first element of $m$.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Composition Formula with Binomial Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k l : ℕ),
  Polynomial.hasseDeriv k ∘ₗ Polynomial.hasseDeriv l = (k + l).choose k • Polynomial.hasseDeriv (k + l)
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $ and natural numbers $ k, l $, the composition of the $ k $-th and $ l $-th Hasse derivatives on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ equals $ \binom{k + l}{k} $ times the $ (k + l) $-th Hasse derivative, i.e., $ D^{(k)} \circ D^{(l)} = \binom{k + l}{k} D^{(k + l)} $.

items.informal_name: Factorial Scaling of Hasse Derivative Equals Iterated Derivative
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ), ⇑(k.factorial • Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) = (⇑Polynomial.derivative)^[k]
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative operator on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $, when multiplied by $ k! $, equals the $ k $-th iterate of the standard derivative operator. Formally, $ k! \cdot D^{(k)} = (\frac{d}{dX})^k $, where $ D^{(k)} $ denotes the Hasse derivative of order $ k $.

items.informal_name: Successor Case for Iterated Partial Derivatives in Schwartz Space
items.type:
∀ {V : Type u_14} {E : Type u_15} [inst : LineDeriv V E E] {n : ℕ} (m : Fin (n + 1) → V) (f : E),
  LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp m f = LineDeriv.lineDerivOp (m 0) (LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp (Fin.tail m) f)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, a map $m : \mathrm{Fin}(n+1) \to V$, and $f \in E$, the $(n+1)$-th iterated linear derivative $\mathrm{LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp}(m, f)$ equals the composition of the first derivative $\mathrm{LineDeriv.lineDerivOp}(m(0), \cdot)$ with the $n$-th iterated derivative $\mathrm{LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp}(\mathrm{Fin.tail}(m), f)$. This expresses the recursive structure of iterated derivatives in Schwartz space.

items.informal_name: Successor Decomposition of Iterated Linear Derivatives
items.type:
∀ {V : Type u_14} {E : Type u_15} [inst : LineDeriv V E E] {n : ℕ} (m : Fin (n + 1) → V) (f : E),
  LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp m f =
    LineDeriv.iteratedLineDerivOp (Fin.init m) (LineDeriv.lineDerivOp (m (Fin.last n)) f)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, function $m : \text{Fin}(n+1) \to V$, and element $f \in E$, the iterated linear derivative $\partial^m f$ equals the composition of the linear derivative $\partial^{\text{init} \, m}$ applied to $\partial_{m(\text{last} \, n)} f$, where $\text{init} \, m$ denotes the restriction of $m$ to $\text{Fin}(n)$ and $\text{last} \, n$ denotes the final element of $\text{Fin}(n+1)$.
